column1: # Kotomo conversion corpus (PLAN.md §13.2, §13.3), run on the host by tests/conversion/run.sh.
# Columns: id, mode (chinese, english, japanese, mixed), context (the text before the cursor; only
# English uses it today, as the previous word), input (the letters typed; empty means nothing typed),
# expected (acceptable outputs separated by "|"; a leading "!" means none of those outputs may appear
# within the rank), rank (1, 3, 5; 0 means anywhere), notes.
# A chinese or mixed mode may carry fuzzy-pinyin rules (PLAN §9.6): `chinese+fuzzy:z_zh,n_l` or
# `chinese+fuzzy:all`; the line then runs on a librime build deployed with the rule file the app
# The corpus measures conversion, not key handling: the runner hands the whole input to the engine
# the mode uses today (Chinese and Mixed: librime's set_input, where a space or an apostrophe is a
# syllable delimiter; Japanese: one Mozc session fed letter by letter; English: the English engine
# with the context as the previous word) and ranks the candidate bar's list as the keyboard builds
# Every capability has a positive and a negative line. Every fixed conversion bug adds a line.
# Never tune an engine to one line at the expense of others: the whole corpus runs before and after.
